name: AirTrunk Malaysia hyperscale platform (JHB1-JHB4, Johor Bahru)
location: Iskandar Puteri / Johor Bahru, Malaysia (four campuses: JHB1-JHB4)
description: AirTrunk's Malaysian hyperscale platform: four campuses in Johor Bahru (Iskandar Puteri) totalling more than 700 MW of IT capacity and about USD 6.8 billion (MYR 27 billion) of committed investment — the anchor data-centre supply for the Johor-Singapore AI corridor. JHB1 (150+ MW, 20 data halls, 132 kV, design PUE 1.15) opened 30 July 2024 with one of the world's largest direct-to-chip liquid-cooling deployments and its remaining ~100 MW of phases began construction August 2024 (initial tranche mid-2025); JHB2 (scalable to 270+ MW, 275 kV, announced 12 February 2025) carries USD 2.325 billion of green financing raised July 2026 (largest single-asset data-centre green financing in Malaysia, first IFC financing, 30 lenders); JHB3 (138+ MW) and JHB4 (142+ MW) were announced 30 April 2026 under a MYR 12 billion (USD 3 billion) investment, powered by 275 kV dual feeds from JHB2. JHB1 and JHB2 (420+ MW combined) were reported almost 100% contracted at the JHB3/JHB4 announcement.

capacities.basis: combined across four campuses; total committed investment about USD 6.8 billion (MYR 27 billion)

150+ MW on 10.3 ha, 21,900 m2 technical data hall area, 20 data halls, 132 kV diverse feeds, design PUE 1.15, 20 MW+ direct-to-chip liquid cooling in flight; flagship 150 MW opened 30 July 2024; remaining ~100 MW of phases under construction from August 2024 (initial tranche mid-2025, A$1 billion+ investment, 2,500+ construction jobs); DTC cooling cuts energy use up to 23%
